sentences.text: The fossil shows a body plan that closely matches the genus Pavo, a group of birds that no longer lives in Taiwan.
It was significantly larger than any modern galliform bird in Taiwan, reaching a size comparable to the largest living peafowls.
The remains were uncovered by private collector L.-R. Hou in the Chiting Formation of Tainan City, Taiwan.
Its presence extends the known range of the genus Pavo to the easternmost part of Asia.
The Paleobiology Database currently lists records for the genus Pavo but has no specific entry for Pavo miejue.
